checks: Resumed verification; first-run absence evidence is retained in phase3-initial-baseline.json
Running Worker core images contain no Inventory package
Inventory is a separately built, versioned, signed immutable OCI package
worker-1: persisted Inventory supports browser creation/editing of real persistent records
worker-3: persisted Inventory supports browser creation/editing of real persistent records
Worker 2 remains module-free and unchanged; Worker 1/3 records, databases, and configuration are isolated
Every core image hash, container ID, and start time is unchanged during publication, installation, activation, and CRUD
Concurrent and repeated installation requests preserve one installation and one immutable module container
Unauthenticated, cross-Worker-session, invalid-configuration, and CSRF requests are rejected
Tampered/unknown-publisher packages, incompatible platform versions, and missing dependencies are rejected before provisioning
Worker-local module users require explicit API grants; read-only users can list but cannot write or administer, in API and browser
Deactivation stops the module and hides/rejects its API while preserving records; reactivation restores access
Real failing SQL migration reports failed state, rolls back its uncommitted transaction, and explicitly recovers with corrected signed version; databases are never dropped
Provider verifies TLS identity and Worker signatures, rejects exact replay, stale/wrong-installation/altered proofs; sensitive v3 routes are absent on HTTP
Module has only its own read-only secret subpath, no published port/socket/core credentials, isolated networks, and no permission to connect to the Worker core database
Worker and module-host restarts preserve enrollment, local administrator session, module configuration, activation, and inventory records without Master login
All Workers remain healthy/ready with the entire Master stack stopped; Inventory API writes and browser reads continue
Browser installation and CRUD flows have no uncaught JavaScript errors
All three companies create and edit persistent operational records independently through Chromium
Master exposes entity-scoped analytical copies, organization relationships, operating entity, record/event provenance and freshness
Inventory retains old records, displays 800 stock / 200 reserved / 600 available and synchronizes its declared stock projection
Repeated real events deduplicate; older revisions never overwrite newer data; same-revision conflicts are rejected
Signed cross-entity claims, unauthorized analytical access, cross-Worker sessions, stale and replayed transport proofs are rejected
Master outage does not block operational writes; durable module outboxes and committed records survive Worker SIGKILL/restart
Killing a PostgreSQL transaction rolls back both its operational write and triggered outbox event atomically
SIGKILL during an in-flight exchange resumes safely; outage changes catch up incrementally with one inbox entry per event
Master issues a finding through Chromium; only affected Workers receive it, with entity-filtered supporting references
Controlled redelivery of actual finding events creates no duplicate local findings and is durably acknowledged
Offline finding acknowledgment survives process restart, synchronizes back to Master, rejects stale edits and survives later Master lifecycle updates
Original installation configuration, enrolled Worker 1 certificate and every pre-existing Inventory record remain intact
All installations remain healthy with their original identities; Chromium has zero uncaught errors
